topic: Understanding Distribution Channels – Concept & Progress
t: 'Place' in the marketing mix (4 Ps) corresponds to decisions about:
e: Place covers how the product reaches the customer: channel selection, coverage, locations and logistics. Promotion, product and price are the other three Ps.

topic: Understanding Distribution Channels – Concept & Progress
t: The Malhotra Committee (1994) is significant for Indian insurance distribution because it:
o: Recommended opening the sector to private and foreign players, leading to new channels after 2000
Set the first commission rates for agents
e: The Malhotra Committee's recommendations led to the IRDA Act, 1999 and the entry of private insurers, which in turn created corporate agency, broking and other channels.

topic: Channel Mix Decisions and Distribution Strategy
t: Which of the following is NOT typically a criterion for evaluating alternative channels?
e: Channel alternatives are compared on economic performance, degree of control and adaptability (commitment period). Packaging colour is a product decision, not a channel criterion.

topic: Channel Mix Decisions and Distribution Strategy
t: A health insurer wants to retain pricing control, build its brand and gather customer data directly. It also wants volume quickly at low fixed cost. Which channel combination best balances these goals?
o: Only exclusive dealership with one bank
Direct online channel plus corporate agents
e: A direct channel offers control and data; corporate agents offer rapid volume at variable cost. Combining them is a typical multi-channel trade-off between control and reach.

topic: Channel Mix Decisions and Distribution Strategy
t: Which of the following is a common method of resolving channel conflict?
o: Paying identical commission regardless of performance
Ending all communication with channel members
Adopting superordinate goals that all members accept
e: Conflict management tools include superordinate goals, exchange of personnel, co-optation, joint membership of associations, mediation and arbitration.

topic: Channel Mix Decisions and Distribution Strategy
t: 'Channel margin' in insurance distribution most closely corresponds to:
o: The commission or remuneration paid to the intermediary out of the premium
e: The intermediary's reward for performing distribution functions is its margin; in insurance it is the commission/remuneration, now governed by the insurer's board-approved policy within EoM limits.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: The examination for individual insurance agents in India is conducted by:
o: The examination body designated by IRDAI (the Insurance Institute of India)
e: Agents must pass the examination of the IRDAI-recognised examination body (III); POSPs, by contrast, are examined by the engaging insurer or intermediary.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: Under Section 42 of the Insurance Act, 1938, a person who acts as an insurance agent without a valid appointment is liable to a penalty of up to:
e: The individual faces a penalty up to ₹10,000, whereas an insurer appointing an agent in contravention of the Act may be penalised up to ₹1 crore.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: Which of the following is a requirement for a corporate agent whose insurance distribution is its ONLY business?
o: Minimum net worth of ₹50 lakh at all times
e: Exclusive corporate agents must maintain ₹50 lakh net worth; entities with other main businesses (e.g. banks) have no separate minimum. ₹5 crore is the composite broker capital and ₹10 lakh is the direct broker deposit.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: Under the IRDAI (Insurance Brokers) Regulations, 2018, the minimum paid-up capital for a direct insurance broker is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Direct brokers need ₹75 lakh capital; reinsurance brokers ₹4 crore and composite brokers ₹5 crore. ₹25 lakh is the web-aggregator capital and ₹50 lakh is the direct broker's minimum net worth.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: A corporate agent earns ₹8 crore in insurance remuneration in a year, out of total revenue of ₹12 crore. Which statement is CORRECT regarding professional indemnity (PI) insurance?
o: PI cover is required because insurance remuneration exceeds 50% of total revenue, with a limit of twice the annual remuneration subject to prescribed minimum and maximum
No PI cover is required because the entity is not a broker
PI cover is required only for brokers earning above ₹5 crore
PI cover must be exactly ₹8 crore
e: Insurance is 66.7% of revenue, which exceeds the 50% threshold triggering the PI requirement for corporate agents; the limit is 2× remuneration within the ₹15 lakh–₹1 crore band.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: A broker's minimum professional indemnity cover for a direct broker is:
e: Direct brokers must hold PI cover of twice annual remuneration subject to a minimum of ₹1 crore; reinsurance brokers ₹4 crore and composite brokers ₹5 crore minimum.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: Which of the following is a MERIT of the tied agency channel?
o: Lowest acquisition cost of all channels
Face-to-face need analysis, personalised advice and ongoing servicing relationship
e: Agents provide advice and relationship continuity that help in selling complex, long-term products. Agency is, however, costly and slow to build.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: A 'fully integrated' bancassurance model is one in which:
o: The bank owns or holds a significant stake in the insurer and the two share systems, staff and strategy
The insurer sells through the bank's ATM screens only
The bank simply refers leads for a fee
The bank acts as a corporate agent of an unrelated insurer
e: Bancassurance models range from referral and corporate agency (distribution alliance) to joint ventures and full integration where the bank is promoter of the insurer.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: Which of the following is NOT permitted for a web aggregator?
o: Acting as a corporate agent of an insurer simultaneously
Carrying out permitted outsourcing functions such as tele-marketing and premium reminders for insurers
Displaying product comparisons of multiple insurers
e: A web aggregator cannot concurrently hold another intermediary registration such as corporate agency; it may compare products, pass leads and perform permitted outsourcing/tele-marketing services.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: A life insurer's 13th-month persistency ratio of 72% (by number of policies) means that:
o: 72% of claims were settled within 13 months
72% of the policies sold a year earlier were still in force after the first renewal premium fell due
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Persistency measures retention of policies at a specified duration. Low 13th-month persistency indicates mis-selling or poor need analysis at the point of sale.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: An Insurance Sales Person (ISP) of an IMF must have at least:
e: ISPs need 12th standard; the IMF's Principal Officer must be at least a graduate. Individual agents and POSPs need only 10th standard.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: The POSP examination is conducted by:
o: The insurer or intermediary engaging the POSP, after 15 hours of in-house training
e: Unlike regular agents, POSPs are trained (15 hours) and examined in-house by the engaging insurer or intermediary, which keeps the channel low-cost.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: A key demerit of the online direct channel for a life insurer is:
o: Low conversion for products needing advice and difficulty in explaining complex features
e: Online works for simple products; for complex, high-ticket plans customers often abandon the journey or need human assistance, so insurers add call-centre support ('phygital').

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: Common Service Centres (CSCs) distribute insurance in rural India through:
o: Village Level Entrepreneurs registered as Rural Authorised Persons under the CSC-SPV arrangement with IRDAI
e: IRDAI guidelines allow CSC-SPV to act as an intermediary, with trained Village Level Entrepreneurs (RAPs) selling simple products such as motor, PA and crop-related covers.

topic: Creating Customer Value through Distribution
t: 'Total customer benefit' in Kotler's value framework includes all of the following EXCEPT:
e: Benefits are product, service, personnel and image; time cost belongs to total customer cost. Value = total benefit − total cost.

topic: Creating Customer Value through Distribution
t: The SERVQUAL dimension 'reliability' means:
o: Performing the promised service dependably and accurately
e: Reliability is the most important dimension for most services: doing what was promised, e.g. issuing the policy and paying the claim correctly and on time.

topic: Creating Customer Value through Distribution
t: A 'value proposition' is:
o: The whole cluster of benefits the company promises to deliver to the customer
The list of exclusions in a policy
e: The value proposition summarises why a customer should buy from a company; distribution channels must deliver this promise consistently at every touch point.

topic: Creating Customer Value through Distribution
t: An agent explains the claims process clearly, hands over the policy personally within a week and calls after 30 days to check understanding. In SERVQUAL terms, these actions mainly strengthen:
e: Timely delivery (reliability), prompt attention (responsiveness) and caring follow-up (empathy) raise perceived service quality and therefore customer value.

topic: Creating Customer Value through Distribution
t: Which of the following is a 'psychic cost' for an insurance buyer?
o: The anxiety and worry of possibly choosing the wrong policy
e: Psychic cost is the mental stress or anxiety attached to a purchase; a trusted advisor reduces it, which is a central way distribution creates value in insurance.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: 'Inseparability' of services means that:
o: The policy cannot be split between nominees
Insurers cannot be separated from reinsurers
Premium cannot be paid in instalments
Production and consumption of the service occur together, so the distributor's behaviour is part of the product experience
e: In services the provider and the customer interact at the moment of delivery; in insurance the agent's advice and conduct are inseparable from the customer's experience of the product.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: Which statement about the insurance sales cycle is CORRECT?
o: Motor insurance has a 10-year policy term
General insurance renewals are an annual opportunity for the channel to re-engage, whereas regular-premium life policies need multi-year servicing
e: Most general and health policies are annual, creating recurring renewal touch points; life policies are long term with premiums payable over many years, so persistency management matters.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: An insurer's total premium is ₹60,000 crore and the country's GDP is ₹3,00,00,000 crore (₹300 lakh crore). What is this insurer's contribution to insurance penetration?
e: ₹60,000 crore ÷ ₹3,00,00,000 crore = 0.002 = 0.2%. Penetration expresses premium as a share of GDP.

topic: Understanding Distribution Channels – Concept & Progress
t: Before the opening of the Indian insurance sector in 2000, life insurance distribution in India was dominated by:
o: The individual tied agency force of LIC
Bank branches acting as corporate agents
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Until liberalisation, LIC's large individual agency force was effectively the only life distribution channel. Corporate agents, brokers and aggregators were introduced by IRDAI regulations after 2000.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: Mis-selling in insurance distribution is MOST likely when:
o: The distributor is paid on persistency
The insurer conducts a verification call
The distributor is paid high upfront incentives with no clawback and has sales targets unrelated to customer needs
e: Front-loaded incentives without accountability for policy continuance create the classic incentive for mis-selling; persistency linkage, fact-finds and PIVC are counter-measures.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: 'Embedded insurance' refers to:
o: A policy printed inside a bank passbook
Insurance offered as part of another product or service purchase (e.g. travel cover at ticket booking, device cover at checkout)
Insurance sold only through embedded agents
e: Embedded insurance uses digital platforms and APIs to bundle cover with another transaction, a growing distribution opportunity in e-commerce, travel and fintech.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: Which of the following is a reason health insurance distribution faces special challenges?
o: Pre-existing disease waiting periods, room-rent limits and co-pays are difficult to explain, leading to claim-stage disputes
Health insurance cannot be sold by agents
e: Health products have many conditions; inadequate explanation at sale leads to dissatisfaction at claim time, placing a premium on clear disclosure by the channel.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: 'Phygital' distribution in insurance means:
o: Combining digital tools with physical human assistance across the customer journey
e: Phygital models use digital lead generation, e-proposals and e-KYC, supported by agents or call-centre staff for advice and closure, addressing the limits of pure online selling.

topic: Customer Relationship Management through Distribution
t: 'Collaborative CRM' refers to:
o: Sharing customer information and coordinating interactions across departments, channels and partners
e: Collaborative CRM integrates touch points (agents, branches, call centre, web) so that the customer gets a consistent experience regardless of channel.

topic: Health insurance norms
t: The maximum waiting period for pre-existing diseases in health insurance, after the 2024 IRDAI changes, is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Reduced from 48 to 36 months; the moratorium period after which claims cannot be contested (except fraud) is 60 months.

topic: Customer Relationship Management through Distribution
t: An insurer estimates that a customer pays ₹30,000 premium a year, the contribution margin is 10%, and the expected relationship is 15 years (ignoring discounting). The approximate customer lifetime value is:
e: ₹30,000 × 10% = ₹3,000 per year × 15 years = ₹45,000. Discounting would reduce this; ₹4,50,000 is total premium, not contribution.

topic: Customer Relationship Management through Distribution
t: 'Customer churn' in insurance refers to:
o: Customers discontinuing their relationship by lapsing, surrendering or not renewing
e: Churn is the rate at which customers leave; analytical CRM builds churn-propensity models so that the channel can intervene before lapse or non-renewal.

topic: Customer Relationship Management through Distribution
t: Which of the following is an example of up-selling by an agent?
o: Recommending that a customer raise the sum insured of an existing health policy from ₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh
Selling a motor policy to a term-life customer
e: Up-selling increases the value of the same product line (higher cover or add-on riders); cross-selling adds a different product category.

topic: Customer Relationship Management through Distribution
t: 'Customer segmentation' in CRM is useful to a distribution manager because it:
o: Helps allocate channel effort and tailor products and communication to groups with similar needs and value
Allows identical treatment of all customers
Eliminates the need for sales staff
e: Segmenting by value, life stage, needs or behaviour lets the insurer match channels (e.g. advisor-led for HNI, digital for young salaried) to customer groups.

topic: Best Practices in Distribution Management in Insurance
t: Which of the following is a best practice in agent compensation design?
o: Paying the entire reward in the first year only
Balancing first-year commission with renewal commission and persistency-linked rewards
Paying commission in cash to avoid records
Linking commission to the number of policies surrendered
e: A balanced structure rewards both acquisition and continuation; it discourages churning and builds long-term agent income and customer retention.

topic: Best Practices in Distribution Management in Insurance
t: 'Activity management' in agency distribution refers to:
o: Planning and tracking the agent's prospecting calls, appointments, fact-finds and closures to improve productivity
e: Activity management uses funnel ratios (calls to appointments to closes) so that managers coach agents on specific weaknesses rather than only on results.

topic: Best Practices in Distribution Management in Insurance
t: A 'welcome call' made by the insurer after policy issue serves to:
o: Confirm receipt of the policy document, reiterate free-look rights and detect any mis-selling early
e: Welcome calls are a post-issuance control that reinforce understanding and give customers a chance to raise concerns within the free-look period.

topic: Best Practices in Distribution Management in Insurance
t: Which of the following is an agent obliged to do under the code of conduct?
o: Accept premium in his own name
Disclose the scales of commission to the prospect if asked
Fill the proposal form without consulting the prospect
Guarantee bonus rates in participating policies
e: The code requires disclosure of commission scales on request, explanation of the product and of material information requirements, and prohibits guaranteeing returns or misleading statements.

topic: Best Practices in Distribution Management in Insurance
t: An agency manager has 40 agents of whom 12 produced no business in the last quarter. The best-practice response is to:
o: Analyse causes (activity levels, skill gaps, market), provide coaching and set activity plans, and exit only chronic non-performers
Ignore them since they cost nothing
Transfer their policies to the manager
e: Agency management best practice treats non-production as a diagnosis problem first; structured coaching reduces attrition and protects orphan-policy servicing.

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: The 'Bima Trinity' announced by IRDAI consists of:
o: Bima Bharosa, Bima Lokpal and Bima Sugam
Bima Sugam, Bima Vistaar and Bima Vahak
e: The three complementary initiatives: an electronic marketplace (Bima Sugam), a composite affordable product (Bima Vistaar) and a women-centric field force (Bima Vahak).

topic: Intermediaries
t: The qualifying examination for an individual insurance agent conducted by the Insurance Institute of India is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). IC-38 is the agents' pre-recruitment examination; IC-01/02/11/14 are Licentiate papers.

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: 'Bima Bharosa' is:
o: An IRDAI integrated grievance management portal for policyholders
e: Bima Bharosa (formerly IGMS) lets policyholders lodge and track complaints against insurers; it supports the regulator's consumer-protection objectives.

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: IRDAI's 'Use and File' procedure allows insurers to:
o: File claims directly with the regulator
Launch most products and then file them with IRDAI, instead of waiting for prior approval
e: Use and File (extended in 2022) speeds up product launches for most life, general and health products, supporting innovation and faster distribution of new covers.

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: A standalone health insurer writes ₹1,200 crore gross premium in a year. Under the EoM regulations its allowable expenses of management are up to:
e: Standalone health insurers are allowed 35% of gross written premium: 35% × ₹1,200 crore = ₹420 crore. General insurers get 30% (₹360 crore).

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: Under the 2022 amendment, the area of operation permitted to an Insurance Marketing Firm was expanded from:
o: A State to the whole country
A district to the whole State/UT in which it is registered
e: IMFs were originally restricted to a district; the 2022 reforms allowed operation across the State, improving viability alongside the increase in insurer tie-ups to six per category.
